reason: The text depicts both the Israelites and Moses as agents who make choices and initiate action. The Israelites actively quarrel (וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־ מֹשֶׁה) and demand water (תְּנוּ־ לָנוּ מַיִם וְנִשְׁתֶּה). They vocalize complaints (וַיָּלֶן הָעָם עַל־ מֹשֶׁה) and challenge Moses about bringing them from Egypt. Moses responds with reasoning (מַה־ תְּרִיבוּן עִמָּדִי), intercedes with God (וַיִּצְעַק מֹשֶׁה אֶל־ יְהוָה), and executes God's instructions (וַיַּעַשׂ כֵּן מֹשֶׁה). The narrative structure shows people initiating dialogue, expressing needs, and taking deliberate actions rather than passively receiving events. Even though God's power frames the narrative, human characters demonstrably exercise agency within it.
